Q: Can ggplot theme formatting be saved as an object? A:

The other answers are already very good, but I wanted to add that for those attempting to apply a theme preset, such as theme_minimal or theme_bw, you can simply call set_theme to apply to the most recent plot. Easy to combine both into a function to run after you generate the ggplot object and before you send it to the viewer:

set_user_theme <- function() {
    set_theme(theme_bw())
    update_theme(text=element_text(size=24))
}
p <- data %>% 
    ggplot() + 
    .....

set_user_theme()
p

Q: How Can I Exclude Holidays Using My Custom Holiday Table Into my SQL Code that Excludes Weekends A:

The following steps show how we can approach it step by step.

Prepare test data

CREATE TABLE dbo.Contacts(
    ContactID   INT        NOT NULL,
    ContactType VARCHAR(8) NOT NULL,
    ContactDate DATE       NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE dbo.Holidays(
    HolidayDesc VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    HolidayDate DATE        NOT NULL
);
GO
INSERT dbo.Contacts(ContactID, ContactType, ContactDate)
VALUES (12345, 'TYPE1', '6/18/2026'),
       (12345, 'TYPE2', '6/25/2026'),
       (67890, 'TYPE1', '6/18/2026'),
       (67890, 'TYPE2', '6/24/2026');
INSERT dbo.Holidays(HolidayDesc, HolidayDate)
VALUES ('Juneteenth', '6/19/2026'),
       ('Independence Day', '7/3/2026');

List the dates from the date of TYPE1 to the date of TYPE2

SELECT c1.ContactID,
       DATEADD(DAY, v.number, c1.ContactDate) AS Date
FROM   dbo.Contacts       AS c1
JOIN   dbo.Contacts       AS c2 ON c1.ContactID = c2.ContactID AND c2.ContactType = 'TYPE2'
JOIN   master..spt_values AS v  ON v.type = 'P'
   AND v.number BETWEEN 1 AND DATEDIFF(DAY, c1.ContactDate, c2.ContactDate)
WHERE  c1.ContactType = 'TYPE1';

Output:

ContactID   Date
----------- ----------
12345       2026-06-19
12345       2026-06-20
12345       2026-06-21
12345       2026-06-22
12345       2026-06-23
12345       2026-06-24
12345       2026-06-25
67890       2026-06-19
67890       2026-06-20
67890       2026-06-21
67890       2026-06-22
67890       2026-06-23
67890       2026-06-24

Here we can leverage the system table master..spt_values which comes with various sequences of convenient numbers. When type column equals 'P', the value of number column would be a sequence from 0 to 2047. Using the numbers to add dates can give us a range of 5.6 years, should be more than enough.

See also: Using a Table of Numbers

Note that we skip the starting date of the same ContactID group for ease of counting the dates in the following steps.

Count working days

WITH Dates AS (
    SELECT c1.ContactID,
           DATEADD(DAY, v.number, c1.ContactDate) AS Date
    FROM   dbo.Contacts       AS c1
    JOIN   dbo.Contacts       AS c2 ON c1.ContactID = c2.ContactID AND c2.ContactType = 'TYPE2'
    JOIN   master..spt_values AS v  ON v.type = 'P'
       AND v.number BETWEEN 1 AND DATEDIFF(DAY, c1.ContactDate, c2.ContactDate)
    WHERE  c1.ContactType = 'TYPE1'
)
SELECT d.ContactID,
       COUNT(*) AS CountWorkDays
FROM   Dates AS d
WHERE  DATENAME(WEEKDAY, d.Date) NOT IN ('Saturday','Sunday')
   AND NOT EXISTS (
       SELECT 1
       FROM   dbo.Holidays AS h
       WHERE  h.HolidayDate = d.Date
   )
GROUP  BY d.ContactID;

Output:

ContactID   CountWorkDays
----------- -------------
12345       4
67890       3

Use the last result as a CTE to generate 'Yes' / 'No' result

WITH Dates AS (
    SELECT c1.ContactID,
           DATEADD(DAY, v.number, c1.ContactDate) AS Date
    FROM   dbo.Contacts       AS c1
    JOIN   dbo.Contacts       AS c2 ON c1.ContactID = c2.ContactID AND c2.ContactType = 'TYPE2'
    JOIN   master..spt_values AS v  ON v.type = 'P'
       AND v.number BETWEEN 1 AND DATEDIFF(DAY, c1.ContactDate, c2.ContactDate)
    WHERE  c1.ContactType = 'TYPE1'
),
WorkDaysCount AS (
    SELECT d.ContactID,
           COUNT(*) AS CountWorkDays
    FROM   Dates AS d
    WHERE  DATENAME(WEEKDAY, d.Date) NOT IN ('Saturday','Sunday')
       AND NOT EXISTS (
           SELECT 1
           FROM   dbo.Holidays AS h
           WHERE  h.HolidayDate = d.Date
       )
    GROUP  BY d.ContactID
)
SELECT c.ContactID,
       c.ContactType,
       c.ContactDate,
       CASE WHEN w.CountWorkDays <= 3 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS Day3Validate
FROM   dbo.Contacts AS c
JOIN   WorkDaysCount AS w ON c.ContactID = w.ContactID
WHERE  c.ContactType = 'TYPE2';

Output:

ContactID   ContactType ContactDate Day3Validate
----------- ----------- ----------- ------------
12345       TYPE2       2026-06-25  No
67890       TYPE2       2026-06-24  Yes

A more portable solution

Using the undocumented master..spt_values system table could be a problem if in the future it is removed from a new release of SQL Server. It's also not supported by other RDBMS. To write a more portable query, we need to generate a number series on-the-fly. In the following example query the numbers range from 1 to 10,000, should be enough to support 27 years of data.

WITH T1(F) AS (
    SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL 
    SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL 
    SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1
),                      
T2(F) AS (SELECT 1 FROM T1 AS A, T1 AS B),
T3(F) AS (SELECT 1 FROM T2 AS A, T2 AS B),
T4(F) AS (SELECT 1 FROM T3 AS A, T3 AS B),
Numbers(number) AS (
    SELECT TOP(10000) ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT NULL))
    FROM   T4
),
Dates AS (
    SELECT c1.ContactID,
           DATEADD(DAY, n.number, c1.ContactDate) AS Date
    FROM   dbo.Contacts AS c1
    JOIN   dbo.Contacts AS c2 ON c1.ContactID = c2.ContactID AND c2.ContactType = 'TYPE2'
    JOIN   Numbers      AS n  ON n.number <= DATEDIFF(DAY, c1.ContactDate, c2.ContactDate)
    WHERE  c1.ContactType = 'TYPE1'
),
WorkDaysCount AS (
    SELECT d.ContactID,
           COUNT(*) AS CountWorkDays
    FROM   Dates AS d
    WHERE  DATENAME(WEEKDAY, d.Date) NOT IN ('Saturday','Sunday')
       AND NOT EXISTS (
           SELECT 1
           FROM   dbo.Holidays AS h
           WHERE  h.HolidayDate = d.Date
       )
    GROUP  BY d.ContactID
)
SELECT c.ContactID,
       c.ContactType,
       c.ContactDate,
       CASE WHEN w.CountWorkDays <= 3 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS Day3Validate
FROM dbo.Contacts  AS c
JOIN WorkDaysCount AS w ON c.ContactID = w.ContactID
WHERE c.ContactType = 'TYPE2';

The technique is documented in: Generate N sequential numbers (fast) - SQLServerCentral

Q: What is the '-->' operator in C/C++? A:

--> is not an operator. It's two separate operators, -- and >, sitting next to each other.

while (x --> 0)     // parsed as:  while ( (x--) > 0 )

The tokenizer uses maximal munch: it grabs the longest valid token first, so --> splits into -- then >. Since whitespace between tokens is insignificant, the compiler sees the same thing as:

while (x-- > 0)

x-- returns the current value of x and then decrements it; that returned value is what gets compared to 0. So the loop runs with x = 10, 9, 8, … 1 and exits when x is 0 (leaving x as -1).

The spacing is just a visual pun, it looks like "x goes to 0."

Q: gganimate::animate() warns "font family not found in Windows font database" even when using ragg A:

The root cause is that {gganimate} and {showtext} use incompatible font rendering paths, and font_add_google() doesn't make fonts visible to the component that needs them.

{showtext} works by hooking into the graphics device at render time and substituting its own font rendering. This works fine for static plots, but animate() with device = "ragg_png" opens a fresh {ragg} device for each frame in a separate rendering pass. Moreover, {ragg} has its own font system ({systemfonts}) that operates independently of {showtext}. When both are active they conflict.

font_add_google() registers fonts in {sysfonts}'s internal registry but it doesn't install them to the Windows font database or to {systemfonts}. So when {gganimate} renders frames through ragg_png, the fonts aren't where {ragg} looks.

{gganimate} builds each frame as a ggplot grob and renders it via the device specified in animate(). Even with device = "ragg_png", grid measures text layout before the device renders; C_textBounds and C_stringMetric are grid's internal C-level calls for computing text dimensions, and on Windows they go through GDI (Graphics Device Interface) for this measurement step regardless of which graphics device is active for rendering. The warnings appear at the layout stage before ragg_png draws anything.

GDI only sees fonts installed on the system (not what font_add_google() does). Static {ggplot2} in the RStudio plot window uses the AGG backend set in Global Options -> General -> Graphics Backend. With {ragg} as the active device it intercepts grid's text measurement calls, so fonts work there. animate() opens its own device per frame outside that context, and grid's measurement calls fall back to GDI.

First, install the fonts so GDI can find them. Download IBM Plex Sans and EB Garamond from fonts.google.com, extract the zip files, select all .ttf files, right-click and install for all users. This puts them in C:\Windows\Fonts. Per-user install (the default double-click) might not be sufficient. I have not tried this, but systemfonts::require_font() should work too (instead of manually installing).

Verify after installing and restarting R:

library(systemfonts)
system_fonts()[grep("EB Garamond|IBM Plex Sans", system_fonts()$family), "path"]
# paths should now show C:\Windows\Fonts\... or AppData\Local\...

Since {ragg} handles fonts via {systemfonts}, {showtext} is not needed. Use the actual font family names instead of the "body" and "title" aliases that only existed in {showtext}'s registry:

library(ggplot2)
library(ggtext)
library(gganimate)
library(ragg)
showtext::showtext_auto(FALSE)  # disable showtext hook

windowsFonts(`IBM Plex Sans` = windowsFont("IBM Plex Sans"),
             `EB Garamond`   = windowsFont("EB Garamond"))

p <- ggplot(AftershocksInSequence,
            aes(x = TimeSincePrimaryEvent, y = magnitude, fill = fact_int_mag)) +
  geom_col(position = "identity") +
  labs(title    = "Title", subtitle = "{frame_time}", caption  = "Caption",
       x = "Time", y = "Magnitude", fill = "Magn.") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    text          = element_text(family = "IBM Plex Sans", color = "white"),
    axis.text     = element_text(color = "white", size = 6),
    axis.title    = element_text(size = 8),
    plot.title    = element_markdown(family = "EB Garamond"),
    plot.subtitle = element_markdown(family = "EB Garamond", 
                                     size = 6, lineheight = 1.1),
    plot.caption  = element_markdown(family = "EB Garamond", 
                                     size = 7, lineheight = 1.0)
  ) +
  transition_time(maxTime)

animate(p, nframes = 10, device = "ragg_png",
        renderer = gifski_renderer(loop = FALSE))

#> Inserting image 10 at 0.90s (100%)...
#> Encoding to gif... done!

windowsFonts() registers an alias with GDI so the font name resolves correctly for grid's text measurement calls. This only works after the fonts are installed.
